key_insight: In α-Zr <a> loops, partial dislocations and fault ribbons govern core stability, while Fe and H favour faulted segments and Sn and Nb favour perfect segments.
engineering_relevance: These atomistic insights can inform models of solute trapping and irradiation-induced microstructure evolution in zirconium nuclear-fuel cladding.
method: Hybrid quantum mechanics/machine learning (QM/ML) modelling of prismatic <a> loops.
Characterisation of nine dislocation line segments across three loop variants.
QM/ML nudged elastic band calculations of glide barriers and faulted-to-perfect transition pathways.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports core geometries, solute-binding preferences and transition mechanisms for nine line segments, but provides no numerical barriers or validation metrics.
watch_item: Atomistic binding preferences and transition pathways require further validation before extrapolation to reactor-scale irradiation behaviour.
paper_title: Comprehensive QM/ML Study of Dislocation Loop Line Segments in α-Zr Part I: <a> Loop Core Geometries, Solute Binding, and Transition Barriers
